title: SSO assertion ordering leads to transient admin scope flip and lossy audit entries
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Summary: A Moneta customer reported an escalation where users intermittently received admin-level scopes after SSO. The symptom was an unexpected "allow" for admin operations in production despite org policy that should deny that scope. Audit logs showed an allow decision but were missing the originating SAML assertion ID and ordering context, making post-incident analysis difficult. This ticket tracks triage, fix, and audit backfill.
reproduction_steps: 1) Configure SAML IdP that emits duplicate attributes (email + external_id) split across two assertions in a single SSO response
2) Map attributes in IdP to RBAC v2 attribute filters (one assertion contains role=admin in claim A; another contains role=member in claim B)
3) Authenticate via SSO -> observe resulting mapped scopes in user session; intermittently admin scopes appear depending on assertion processing order
4) Inspect /v1/auth/decision audit entries for the login - note missing assertion provenance (no assertion_id) and only final merged attributes recorded
impact_summary: High customer impact: Moneta observed potential admin escalation for at least 4 users during peak hours. Compliance group flagged insecure audit trails because assertion provenance was omitted. Potential regulatory exposure for payments customer. Active support escalation and hold on further tenant config changes until remediation.
root_cause: Attribute merge pipeline deduplicates attribute keys by value-first-wins using an unstable iteration over the SAML assertion list. The pipeline did not preserve per-assertion provenance metadata and collapsed attributes without deterministic ordering. When an assertion with admin role appeared later in the IdP response, it could overwrite or be selected depending on iteration order, causing a transient admin scope. Audit writer used the collapsed attribute set and failed to include assertion_id list, producing lossy logs.
mitigation: Hotpatch: set temporary policy to reject any incoming SSO response that contains duplicate attribute keys across assertions for orgs with strict RBAC policies (implemented via gateway filter). Added an emergency audit hook that logs raw SAML assertion payloads (redacted PII) for Moneta for 72h. Instructed customer to enable per-assertion strict validation in IdP until fix is released.
proposed_fix: 1) Change attribute merge semantics to deterministic order: preserve original assertion order from IdP and implement last-wins with opt-in per-org configuration. 2) Attach provenance metadata (assertion_id and assertion_index) to every attribute that contributes to an authorization decision. 3) Update audit writer to emit both merged attrs and provenance array so decisions are explainable. 4) Add unit + integration tests for multi-assertion SSO cases and load test for throughput impact.
rollout_plan:
- Merge PR to staging (runtime-1.22-stg) -> smoke tests against Moneta test tenant
- Canary deploy to 5% of hosted traffic for 48h with increased observation retention
- If stable, ramp to 100% over 6 hours with automatic rollback on error budget breaches
- Run audit backfill job to attach assertion provenance to decisions for the 12h window surrounding known incidents (note: backfill writes a supplemental audit entry, does not mutate original logs)
qa_checks: End-to-end SAML flow with multiple assertions: verified assertion_index preserved in decision trace
Audit entries include assertion_id array and redacted raw assertions for debug tenants
No measurable latency increase >3ms p50 in auth decision path under 95th percentile load
Unit tests for attribute merge ordering and provenance encoding
Security review signoff for temporary raw-assertion logging for Moneta

postmortem_notes: Will capture in incident playbook. Root cause: non-deterministic attribute merge + lossy audit. Action items: (A) enforce deterministic merge across all orgs, (B) include assertion provenance in audit logs, (C) add canary gating for any future auth pipeline changes, (D) improve SSO customer onboarding docs to recommend single-assertion IdP configs for tight RBAC orgs.
